## Factory product asks and tool facts from the owner's M4 long-form (inbox 0740)

Source: `owner-feedback/inbox/2026-10-30-0740-owner-m4-feedback-long-form.md`, items 17, 21, 22 and 23 (owner's words; facts only, no plan item). Item 3 (the orchestrator has no compaction tool and cannot mark the progress log; the owner runs `/compact` at each milestone boundary) is already in "Boundary cost, Droid-Shield and the markdown hook" above and is not repeated.

- Product ask, per-role tool set (item 21): the orchestrator session should launch with only the decision tools. Today R-073 is enforced with a PreToolUse hook on the session id and every denial costs a turn. Ask: a per-role tool set for missions (an orchestrator tools key next to `missionOrchestratorModel`) that removes Execute, Edit, Create, Grep and TodoWrite from the orchestrator's tool definitions only; a session-wide `--remove-tools` would strip the workers' tools too. Owner: "don't try what is not worth it." A per-role tool set in mission settings would make the hook unnecessary.
- Allow-list policy (item 22, applied 20:49): the policy is one sentence, deny whatever is not a decision; `.factory/hooks/officer-decides.sh` applies it to Factory's tools as an allow-list, with unclassified tools denied by default (the allow cases are in "Factory hooks and the rule C hook" above). Observation adds to the policy and never replaces it: a tool seen in the record becomes a finding (a new activity under a decision, or execution that goes to a seat). The hook commit carries its decision file (D-041; the a4b4646 gap).
- Observer overhead ruling FR-P9i (item 23): in-flight only levers on behaviour; product work is a boundary item with its cost. Of the 14 inserted slices at the M4 boundary, 6 were observer-inbox product work (61 worker-minutes, six boundaries); their cost is booked as observer, not M4. The three behaviour levers (rules C, D, E) cost no slice.
- Prompt cache TTL (item 17): the orchestrator prompt cache's TTL is 5 minutes, so every wake after an idle gap longer than that rewrites the whole context before the first token of work. Owner's reading of 29-oct: about 185 orchestrator turns, 65.87 USD-eq since dispatch, of which 46.61 (71 %) is cache writes, 12.47 output and 6.79 cache reads; 17 turns rewrote the whole context (over 100 k tokens written at 12.5 per million, about 2.1 each); a feature takes 10 to 35 minutes, so almost every boundary pays the rewrite. After the levers (rule E, heartbeat): 4 rewrites by the over-50k-written rule (00:30 correction), one a heartbeat-cycle miss (240 s of sleep plus the turn crossed the TTL by about 12 s), so the sleep is 200 s (inbox 0030).
- Product ask, cache TTL (item 17a): a 1-hour cache TTL for the orchestrator session (Anthropic offers it at a higher write price); the owner's estimate is 17 rewrites turned into about 3.
- Keep-warm fact (item 17b): a cheap read turn every 4 minutes while a worker runs would cost about 0.04 (cache read of 170 k) against about 2.1 per rewrite, but the harness's wait returns only at 5 minutes (tool fact of 29-oct morning), so keep-warm under the TTL is not available and the TTL ask stands. Compaction at the boundary halves what each rewrite costs (17c).
EOF
